references.text: Proverbs teaches that the one who gives generously will themselves receive abundantly—the same principle Jesus teaches about giving and receiving.
The one who shows mercy to the poor lends to the Lord, and He will repay them for their good deed. The same principle that God rewards the giver.
The promise that the one who honors the Lord with their wealth will have their barns filled with abundance. Parallel to Jesus' promise of a rich measure returned.
God encourages His people to bring tithes and promises to open the windows of heaven with overflowing blessing—parallel to the overflowing measure in Luke 6:38.
The immediate context: Do not judge, do not condemn, forgive—and you will be forgiven. Verse 38 continues this principle of repayment.
"With the measure you use, it will be measured back to you." Almost a word-for-word parallel to the final sentence in Luke 6:38 about measuring and being measured back.
Jesus says, "The measure you use will be used against you"—parallel to the principle of the repayment measure in Luke 6:38.
Paul applies the same principle: the one who sows sparingly will reap sparingly; the one who sows generously will reap generously. God loves a cheerful giver.
"What a person sows, that they will also reap"—the universal law of repayment underlying Jesus' words in Luke 6:38.
The Philippians gave generously to Paul, and he assures them that God will fill all their needs. An example of the principle of giving and receiving back.
The image of pressing down and shaking a measure to give fully can be linked to the Old Testament picture of the abundance God returns to His faithful ones.
God commands generosity and promises blessing for the one who gives—the same fundamental principle found in Jesus' teaching in Luke 6:38.
